title: Postdoctoral researcher in plant cell biology
description:
Department of Forest Genetics and Plant Physiology

The Department of forest genetics and plant physiology is part of Umeå Plant Science Centre (UPSC, https://www.upsc.se/) which is a centre of excellence for experimental plant research and forest biotechnology in Northern Sweden. Our mission is to perform excellent and innovative basic research and generate knowledge that benefits forestry, agriculture, environment and society. We work across a wide range of disciplines in plant science reaching from cell biology to ecophysiology and from basic research to industrial applications. Our common goal is to understand the plants’ ability to grow, adapt and acclimate to a changing world and how we can breed better plants.

About the position

The long-term goal of our research is to understand the signaling mechanisms regulating plant growth and development (https://www.upsc.se/stephane_vergerhttps://www.upsc.se/stephane_vergerie_robert). You will be part of a team that work at building a better understanding in the signaling controlling cell fate acquisition in Arabidopsis root. The candidate postdoc fellow will aim at dissecting the modes of action of positional information signaling in this process.

The project is a collaborative project including 4 different research groups and is based on cell biology including live confocal microscopy, molecular biology, microfluidics, electrophysiology and cell wall biology.

Your profile

Applicants require a doctoral degree in molecular, cell or developmental biology, or related disciplines. Furthermore, applicants should be proficient in English both verbally and in writing, and should have the ability to work independently as well as in collaboration with others. Experience in confocal microscopy, Arabidopsis, root development is of merit.

As postdoctoral appointments are career-developing positions for junior researchers, we are primarily looking for candidates with a doctoral degree that is three years old at most.

About us

UPSC belongs to two universities, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences and Umeå University. About 200 people from more than 40 different nationalities work here. We host some 30 principal investigators, and our researchers have access to state-of-the-art analytical platforms, unique tree germplasm resources and plant growth facilities. We strive for a collaborative work environment and support our scientists throughout all career stages by providing professional training opportunities and individual career mentoring.

Read more about our benefits and working at SLU by visiting: https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/work-at-slu/

Location:

Department of Forest Genetics and Plant Physiology, SLU, Umeå.

Form of employment:

Temporary employment 24 months, with the possibility of extension.

Scope:

100%

Start date:

As agreed.

Application:

Please submit your application before deadline 08 September 2026. You can submit your application by clicking the button below.

Union representatives:

https://internt.slu.se/en/my-employment/employee-associations/kontaktpersoner-vid-rekrytering/

The Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) has a key role in the development for sustainable life, based on science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and the responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable societal development and good living conditions on our planet. Our main campuses are located in Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, however, the university also operates at research stations, experimental forests and teaching sites throughout Sweden. SLU has around 4,000 employees, 6,000 students and doctoral students and a turnover of over SEK 4,5 billion. We are investing in attractive environments on all of our campuses. We strive to provide a work environment characterised by inclusivity and gender equality, where different experiences generate conversations between people and pave the way for science, creativity and development. Therefore, we welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

title: Finance Officer
company: The Association of People with Disability
description:
Position Summary

The Finance Officer will be responsible for supporting and maintaining the financial operations of APD's Pune office. The role will involve bookkeeping, accounting records, accounts payable and receivable, bank reconciliation, cash-flow monitoring, payroll support, financial reporting, statutory compliance, audit support and grant-related financial documentation.

The Finance Officer will play an important role in ensuring that financial transactions and records are accurate, timely, properly documented and compliant with APD's financial policies and applicable regulations.

The ideal candidate will have strong accounting knowledge, excellent attention to detail, analytical ability and the ability to maintain financial information with a high level of confidentiality and accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting & Bookkeeping

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records, ledgers, invoices, receipts and supporting documentation.
  • Record financial transactions in the accounting system in accordance with organizational procedures.
  • Ensure proper documentation and coding of expenses and transactions.
  • Review financial documents for accuracy, completeness and appropriate approvals.
  • Maintain organized physical and digital financial records.

Accounts Payable & Receivable

  • Process vendor invoices and ensure timely payments in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Track outstanding payments and receivables.
  • Follow up on pending collections and maintain appropriate records.
  • Verify supporting documents before processing financial transactions.
  • Coordinate with vendors and internal departments regarding payment-related queries.

Bank Reconciliation & Cash Management

  • Perform regular bank reconciliations and identify discrepancies.
  • Monitor cash balances and support cash-flow management.
  • Maintain records of petty cash and other financial transactions.
  • Ensure timely recording and reconciliation of financial transactions.

Financial Reporting

  • Assist in preparing monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports.
  • Prepare financial summaries and statements for management review.
  • Provide financial information and analysis to program and management teams as required.
  • Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and highlight significant variances.
  • Support financial forecasting and planning activities.

Budgeting & Grant Finance

  • Assist in preparing departmental and project budgets.
  • Track project and program expenditure against approved budgets.
  • Support grant-related financial reporting and documentation.
  • Maintain proper financial records for donor-funded projects.
  • Coordinate with program teams to ensure appropriate utilization and documentation of project funds.
  • Assist in preparing financial information required by donors and funding partners.

Payroll Support

  • Assist in monthly payroll preparation.
  • Verify payroll-related information and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate with HR and management to ensure accurate and timely salary processing.
  • Maintain appropriate payroll records and confidentiality.

Statutory Compliance

  • Assist in ensuring compliance with applicable accounting, taxation and financial regulations.
  • Support preparation and filing of required tax and compliance documents.
  • Maintain records required for statutory and organizational compliance.
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders and external professionals on compliance matters as required.

Audit Support

  • Provide financial records, schedules and supporting documents required for internal and external audits.
  • Coordinate with auditors and respond to requests for financial documentation.
  • Assist in resolving audit queries and maintaini​ng proper audit trails.
  • Ensure financial records are complete and readily accessible for audit purposes.

Process Improvement & Internal Controls

  • Follow APD's financial policies, procedures and internal control mechanisms.
  • Identify gaps or inefficiencies in accounting and financial processes and suggest improvements.
  • Support implementation of effective financial controls.
  • Ensure proper authorization and documentation of financial transactions.
Maintain confidentiality and security of financial and organizational information.

Requirements

Experience

  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant experience in finance, accounting or bookkeeping.
  • Experience in an NGO/non-profit organization, donor-funded projects or corporate environment will be an advantage.
  • Experience with grant accounting and financial reporting will be an added advantage.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of accounting and bookkeeping principles.
  • Good understanding of financial controls and compliance requirements.
  • Proficiency in accounting software such as Tally, QuickBooks, Xero or similar platforms.
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Strong analytical and numerical skills.
  • High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Good reconciliation and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong documentation and record-management abilities.
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to manage deadlines and multiple financial activities.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • High level of integrity and confidentiality when handling financial information.

Additional Requirements

  • Willingness to support other finance and administrative activities as required.
  • Ability to work effectively in a mission-driven and inclusive organization.
  • Commitment to APD's values of integrity, accountability, excellence, collaboration and diversity.
  • Sensitivity and respect when working with persons with disabilities and other stakeholders.


Benefits

Benefits:
  • Competitive salary commensurate with experience.
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Paid time off and holidays.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth.

title: Technical Lead - South Bank, QLD
description:
At Flight Centre Travel Group (FCTG) our purpose is to 'open up the world for those who want to see'. Every day, we give people all around the world the opportunity to experience something amazing – travel!

As a Technical Lead, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the design, development, and delivery of innovative technical solutions that support customer and business outcomes. You will technically lead a team of engineers, championing modern software engineering practices, and help drive a culture of continuous improvement. Working closely with product teams, architects, and stakeholders, you will influence technical direction while mentoring and developing engineering talent.
You'll be joining Integration Services, the group of teams that power Flight Centre's end-to-end booking experience - spanning supplier integrations, cart and order management, fulfilment, finance system connectivity and our World 360 Rewards loyalty services. The technology is TypeScript and NestJS services as well as other AWS services, such as Lambda with a strong focus on event-driven integration via SNS/SQS and REST/OpenAPI contracts connecting a broad ecosystem of internal and third-party systems.

title: ENROLLMENT SPECIALIST
description:
The Department of Social Services (DSS) is comprised of the administrative units of the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) and the Department of Homeless Services (DHS). HRA is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance. DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self-sufficiency as quickly as possible.

The Supportive Programs and Initiatives' (SPI) Fair Fares Program Division is a Mayoral initiative to subsidize NYCT fares initiative designed to provide accessible discount for NYCT subways and eligible local bus service to low-income families who are in receipt of Cash Assistance, Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program as well as New York City residents who are living at or below the federal poverty line.

Working under direction of the Enrollment Specialist Supervisor for Fair Fares, the Enrollment Specialist will be responsible for the enrollment of consumers at walk-in locations throughout the city. He/she will meet with the consumers, review all necessary documents, access database, and gather all necessary information from the consumer while completing the enrollment and application process. Enrollment will also include scanning all documents into the database. As the Enrollment Specialist the position will be dealing with highly sensitive documents, confidentiality and discretion is important to the role. In this role the enrollment specialist will be responsible for answering questions and providing information about the discount and requirements for the program; review consumers’ documents for completeness; navigate the enrollment database; maintain equipment; and finalize consumers’ complete Fair Fare enrollment application packages.

SPI' Fair Fares Program is recruiting for six (6) Community Associate, to function as Enrollment Specialists, who will:

- Verify and enroll participant referrals daily: Walk-In, electronically and/or telephonically. Review consumer’s documents for completeness; ensure Fair Fares consumers have all necessary paperwork and documentation required to complete the Fair Fares application process. Documentation will be reviewed and authenticated as “official” documentation while maintaining the highest level of confidentiality and discretion. Be required to undergo mandatory specialized training in how to review and authenticate official documentation.

- Review FF database throughout the day and ensure all program consents are signed. Navigate the enrollment database; scan all authenticated official documents into the database; data enter all demographic and relevant consumer information necessary to process the completed application; and ensure that all information is entered accurately.

- Finalize and submit the consumers complete Fair Fare application; review to ensure that all necessary documents and/or other relevant information are obtained from the consumer. Notify consumers of required, missing documentation, and direct those consumers to return the missing information according to program procedure. Be responsible for informing consumers of how to obtain official documents from local, state and/or information for submission of complete applications. Respond to consumer questions and concerns in a timely manner.

- Coordinate communication around site-specific issues under direction from his or her supervisor; responsible for creating, organizing, scheduling, and presenting information to community audiences via public speaking (conducting information sessions and setting up information tables), flyers, brochures, and other relevant mediums. Coordinate efforts to facilitate communications at the various locations throughout the five boroughs of New York City to support consumers in the Fair Fare enrollment process and provide adequate personnel coverage.


Hours/Shift:
Monday – Friday; 9am - 5pm

COMMUNITY ASSOCIATE - 56057

Qualification Requirements
1. High school graduation or equivalent and three years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to duties described above; or
2. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" above.

The City of New York is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce and providing a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment based upon any legally protected status or protected characteristic, including but not limited to an individual's sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity, or pregnancy.

title: E-Expert Technieker

title: Lead Product Manager - Healthcare Categories
description:
About Numan
Founded in 2018, we’ve already grown to be a 300+ team distributed across the globe, united by a singular mission: empowering people to take control of their health.
Numan is transforming health: we’ve built a cutting-edge platform that integrates diagnostics, medication, supplements, digital programmes, and doctor consultations. Giving people the tools they need to maximise life.
To deliver on our transformative mission, we are guided by our 5 company values:
• Patients first.
• Learn fast.
• Own the quality.
• Succeed together.
• Care deeply.
Backed by top-tier investors, Numan is already having a positive impact on hundreds of thousands of patients here in the UK, and we want you to help us deliver this mission!

The Role

We're looking for an exceptional Product Lead to drive commercial growth across acquisition, conversion and retention for our Obesity category.

Numan operates at an interesting intersection of consumer product, healthcare and commerce. Growing effectively means creating experiences that convert better and retain patients for longer, while maintaining clinical safety, patient trust and the standards expected of a regulated healthcare business.

This role will lead product across some of the most commercially important parts of that system, from how prospective patients understand and enter Numan, through to how we improve conversion, proposition performance, retention and long-term patient value.

You'll work directly across Product, Design, Engineering, Clinical and Commercial teams, turning company priorities and complex constraints into clear product choices and measurable outcomes. You'll be expected to make strong calls in an environment where opportunities move quickly, regulation changes, commercial pressure is real, and the right answer often requires balancing several competing forms of value.

We're looking for someone with exceptional commercial product judgement, strong product craft, and the ability to move fluidly between strategy, discovery and hands-on execution.


You'll be:

  • Turning company strategy and commercial priorities into a defensible product roadmap across acquisition, conversion and retention.

  • Making the calls where commercial opportunity, patient need, clinical safety and execution risk intersect.

  • Owning the successful delivery and performance of the Obesity product area, with clear accountability for measurable commercial and patient outcomes.

  • Understanding Numan's regulated clinical environment deeply enough to grow commercially while protecting patient safety and compliance.

  • Using AI personally to increase the quality and speed of your own work, not simply managing teams that build AI features.

  • Succeeding through the quality of both your decisions and the environment you create around them.


You'll have:

  • Experience leading product for consumer digital products, with direct accountability for acquisition, conversion or retention outcomes.

  • Experience working in regulated environments and translating regulatory or clinical requirements into product decisions.

  • A clear sense of when experimentation is valuable and when conviction and speed are more appropriate.

  • Exceptional product judgement and the ability to make difficult trade-offs in ambiguous environments, with the confidence to defend what the team will and won't do.

  • Evidence of personally using AI to materially improve how you work.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills across executive, commercial, clinical and technical audiences.


It's a bonus if you have:

  • Experience in digital healthcare.

  • Experience with subscription, recurring-revenue or direct-to-consumer business models.

  • Experience using AI-native workflows to design, prototype and ship product experiences end to end.

  • Experience owning a product experience end-to-end (e.g. acquisition and retention).

The Division of Administration Bureau of Human Resources and Labor Relations provides effective human resource management by developing and implementing polices, programs and services in support of the values, vision and mission of the agency.

The Labor Relations Specialist will play a critical role in developing and implementing a newly developed conflict resolution component within the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene by helping to create a mechanism to handle and resolve internal conflict. title: Senior Insight Analyst
description:
End‑to‑end ownership. Category expertise. Client challenge and coaching.
Acts as a subject matter expert in assigned categories, leads complex work independently, challenges client hypotheses, and coaches junior analysts. Drives quantify business opportunities (QBOs), sales leads, and a strong feedback culture. This role is a key branching point between people leadership and deep SME / consulting career paths.

About the role

Customer Success Insight teams at NIQ partner with clients to enable faster, smarter decisions through data and insights across FMCG and Tech & Durable industries.

We are looking for a Senior Insight Analyst to join our Global Insights COE, working with major global clients. In this role, you own end‑to‑end analyses, act as a category subject matter expert, and translate research and sales data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.

This role combines advanced analytics, client ownership, and coaching, and represents a key career step with progression into people leadership (Associate Manager, Team Leader) or deep individual contribution (Associate Consultant, Consulting Teams).

Responsibilities

  • Act as the trusted market expert in one or more categories or industry segments.
  • Own client relationships and partner with Consulting Teams on briefings, analyses, and client presentations.
  • Independently run briefings, challenge client hypotheses, and answer complex business questions using fact‑based analysis and the SCQA framework.
  • Lead end‑to‑end storytelling: structure consultative narratives, quantify business opportunities (QBOs), and shape client category strategy.
  • Proactively identify and document QBOs and sales leads in partnership with Consulting Teams and Account Directors.
  • Mentor junior analysts through formal coaching and COE initiatives (e.g., Grow Together, Let’s Practice) and support Customer Success Academy progression.
  • Leverage AI tools (Ask Arthur, Copilot) to accelerate analysis and improve insight quality, aligned with NIQ’s Fast to Adopt mindset.
  • Drive a strong feedback culture through Presentation Quality Rubric (PQR) peer reviews and Touchpoint Net Promoter Score (t‑NPS) client feedback; share best practices across the COE.
  • Contribute to team and NIQ priorities through strategic internal initiatives.

A little bit about you

You are a strategic and analytically strong professional who turns complex data into clear, actionable insights. You lead work end‑to‑end, collaborate effectively across teams, and act as a trusted partner to Consulting Teams and clients.

With curiosity, accountability, and strong commercial acumen, you are comfortable working independently, coaching others, and contributing to both client impact and internal initiatives.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Marketing, Economics, Statistics, or a related field.
  • 4+ years’ experience in Retail, Market Research, or Consulting (or 3+ years working directly with NIQ / GfK data).
  • Hands‑on experience with NIQ Discover, RMS, CPS (or equivalent GfK platforms) strongly preferred.
  • Confidence using AI tools (Copilot, Ask Arthur, ChatGPT) to automate routine work and sharpen insights.
  • Strong storytelling skills, grounded in “so what” thinking and the SCQA framework.
  • Fluent English (C1 or above), written and verbal.
  • Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills.
  • Strong analytical rigour and attention to detail.
  • Excellent presentation, stakeholder, and client communication skills.
  • Proven ability to manage priorities across multiple client workstreams.
  • Comfortable working in multicultural, virtual teams.
  • NIQ Silver Academy accreditation or equivalent certification is an asset.

Our Benefits

title: Director, Horizon Administration
description:
THE SELECTED CANDIDATE WILL BE OFFERED A SALARY BETWEEN $90,000.00 - $100,000.00.

The Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) protects and promotes the safety and well-being of children and families through child welfare and juvenile justice services and community supports. ACS manages community-based supports and foster care services, and provides subsidized child care vouchers. ACS child protection staff respond to allegations of child maltreatment. In juvenile justice, ACS oversees detention, placement and programs for youth in the community.

The Division of Youth and Family Justice (DYFJ) provides a wide range of services and programs for youth at every stage of the juvenile justice process. Our goals are to (a) build stronger and safer communities and advance public safety by preventing juveniles from entering the New York City's juvenile justice system, (b) provide therapeutic treatment and services to youth in our custodial care, and (c) help juveniles access the tools they need to leave the justice system for good. We strive to help families and young people by providing supportive services that are responsive to the needs of individual youth and families.

DYFJ directly operates two secure detention facilities for Juvenile Delinquents, Juvenile Offenders and Adolescent Offenders whose cases are pending in Family Court or the Youth Parts in Supreme Court: Crossroads Juvenile Center in Brooklyn and Horizon Juvenile Center in the Bronx, where youth receive comprehensive services including medical, dental, mental health care, and education.

Specific duties include but not limited to:

- Monitor and conduct analyses of facility staffing to ensure a balanced allocation of staff across work tours, including tracking schedules, overtime, staff on extended leaves, etc.

- Work closely with the Executive Director to monitor administrative contracts for uniforms, cleaning, personnel, administrative matters and submit procurement requests for new needs and/or renewals.

- Manage performance and learning for the Detention center including coordinating and tracking staff professional development, ensuring staff receive mandated trainings, supporting provision of additional trainings, and supporting performance management and evaluations.

- Manage the Housekeeping Unit which is responsible for daily cleaning of the facility, painting, and laundry services for the youth.

- Coordinate with other ACS divisions on items such as repairs and facility maintenance and building security.

- Coordinate with Crossroads counterpart on new initiatives, process improvement to ensure uniformity between sites.

title: Security Officer
description:
Job Title: Security Officer (Multi-Site)

Location: Covering Fareham, Portsmouth, and Southampton

Weekly Hours: 36 hours per week (contracted)

Shift Pattern: Shift times and days will vary depending on site requirements

Pay Rate: £13.45-£14.94 depending on site rate

Reporting to: Contracts Manager

Overview

An exciting opportunity has arisen at Anchor Group Services for an experienced, professional and flexible Security Officer to join our established team as a Security Officer.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced security professional who enjoys working in a variety of environments while benefiting from guaranteed contracted hours. As a Security Officer, you will support a portfolio of shopping centres and commercial sites across the South Coast, helping to maintain safe, secure and welcoming environments for tenants, visitors, contractors and staff.

No two days are the same. You'll work across a range of locations, building valuable experience while becoming an important part of our wider security team.

Sites Covered

This role involves providing security support across a number of locations which may include, but are not limited to:

  • Fareham Shopping Centre, PO16 0PQ
  • The Marlands Shopping Centre, SO14 7SJ
  • Port Solent, PO6 4TP
  • Rams Walk Shopping Centre, GU32 3JA
  • Meridian Shopping Centre, PO9 1UN

The successful candidate must be prepared to travel to support operational requirements across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

  • Protecting the client's people, property and assets in accordance with Assignment Instructions and site-specific procedures.
  • Conducting regular internal and external patrols.
  • Monitoring site activity and maintaining a visible security presence.
  • Providing a safe and secure environment for visitors, retailers, contractors and staff.
  • Preventing and reporting incidents, losses, damage and unauthorised access.
  • Escalating incidents appropriately to site management, the Control Room, Operations Management or Emergency Services where required.
  • Completing accurate reports, incident logs and patrol records.
  • Assisting customers and members of the public in a professional and friendly manner.
  • Responding to customer enquiries and site-related issues efficiently.
  • Supporting planned and short-notice cover requirements across multiple locations.
  • Maintaining professional conduct, appearance and company standards at all times.
  • Working closely with site management and wider security teams to ensure smooth site operations.

Requirements

  • Essential: Valid SIA Door Supervisor (DS) or Security Guarding (SG) Licence.
  • Essential: Valid UK Driving Licence and access to your own vehicle.
  • Preferred: Valid CCTV licence
  • Full 5-year checkable employment history.
  • Previous security experience.
  • Excellent customer service skills.
  • Confidence in handling conflict calmly and professionally.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Flexible approach to working hours, locations and shift patterns.
  • Reliable, punctual and professional attitude.
  • Smart appearance and high personal standards.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Benefits

  • Full uniform provided.
  • Access to nationally recognised training courses through the Anchor Academy.
  • Access to SIA and First Aid training at discounted rates, with financial support available.
  • Auto-Enrolment Pension (if earnings reach the minimum requirement for auto-enrolment).
  • Stream – access to your pay as you earn it.
  • Cycle to Work Scheme.
  • Free 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme, including access to counselling.
  • Hospital Saturday Fund.
  • Reward and Recognition Awards.

What's Next?

If you would like to be considered for this position, APPLY NOW and a member of our recruitment team will be in touch.

Other companies may call this role: Security Officer, Multi-Site Security Officer, Shopping Centre Security Officer, Relief Security Officer, Mobile Security Officer, Security Guard, SIA Security Officer, Security Operative, or Security Enforcement Officer.

Within commuting distance of: Southampton, Fareham, Portsmouth, Gosport, Waterlooville, Havant, Eastleigh, Hedge End, Winchester, Chichester, Petersfield and surrounding South Coast areas.

title: Project Manager
description:
Hours: Full-Time Position – 35 Hours
Work Location: 30-30 Thomson Avenue, LIC, NY 11101

All interested candidates are encouraged to apply. Please include a copy of your Notice of Results, Proof of Filing, or indicate if you are permanent in the title or if you are on the open-competitive Construction Project Manager exam (Exam Nos. 3042 or 5058).

The NYC Department of Design and Construction, Division of Public Buildings, seeks Project Managers. The Project Managers will be responsible for planning, directing, and coordinating construction. The selected candidates will assist with a portfolio of capital design or construction projects throughout the five boroughs. The Project Manager will be assigned projects at various stages of design and construction, and will be the key contact throughout the scoping, design, and construction procurement phase. The Project Managers will utilize the agency’s technical resources to ensure that their projects meet DDC’s Commitment Plan objectives and follow up on completion schedules. The Project Managers will also apprise Sr. Project Managers of scheduling, construction, and design issues; keep costs within budget; liaise between contractors, DDC and sponsor agencies; maintain comprehensive project history files; coordinate project schedules; review projects; address construction and design issues; prepare change orders, project correspondence, and reports.

Please note: All candidates must be currently authorized to work full-time in the United States (U.S.). In compliance with Public Law 99-603, candidates are required to present original documents proving citizenship or the legal right to work in the U.S. DDC is unable to support or sponsor any visa application or visa extension, including but not limited to OPT/STEM visas, H-1B visas, F-1 practical training, permanent residence sponsorship, or any proposed change of visa type. DDC does not offer a training program as required by U.S. immigration law and is not hiring temporary employees. Candidates must have proper work authorization when an employment offer is made.

Additionally, educational credentials must be from a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accredited institution. Credentials from foreign institutions require independent equivalency verification from an approved evaluation service. A list of providers (fees apply) is available at: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcas/downloads/pdf/employment/nyc-dcas-foreign education-evaluation-guide.pdf.

All applicants, including City Employees:
Please go to NYC Government Jobs | Explore Careers | City of New York, go to Search for Open Jobs, and type in the Job ID # listed above. Submit job application as prompted. Do not apply via Employee Self-Service (ESS), e-mail, mail, or fax your resume to DDC directly.

CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MANAGER - 34202

1. A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State’s Department of Education or a recognized accrediting organization, and five years of full-time satisfactory experience managing and/or inspecting one or more construction projects which must have a total cost of at least $300,000 for each of the five years of the required experience; or
2. One year of the experience as described in “1” above and a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university, accredited by regional, national, professional or specialized agencies recognized as accrediting bodies by the U. S. Secretary of Education and by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA), in engineering, engineering technology, architecture, architectural technology, landscape architecture, construction, construction technology, or construction management; or
3. One year of the experience as described in “1” above and a valid license as a professional engineer, registered architect, or registered landscape architect, issued by a board of examining engineers, architects, or landscape architects duly established and qualified pursuant to the laws of any state or territory of the United States; or
4. A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State's Department of Education or a recognized accrediting organization, and a combination of at least two years of experience as described in “1” above and the education as described in “2” above to equal a total of five years of education and experience. Matriculation in an undergraduate college degree program as described in “2” above may be substituted for experience on the basis of 30 semester credits for one year of satisfactory full-time experience up to a maximum of three years of experience.

Note: Candidates must specify for each construction project they worked on: a description of the construction project, the time period they worked on the construction project, and the type of work they performed. Candidates must also specify the money allotted for the project.

Driver License Requirement: At the time of appointment to this position, you must have a motor vehicle driver license valid in the State of New York. If you have moving violations, license suspension or an accident record, you may be disqualified. This license must be maintained for the duration of your employment.

5. For Assignment to Level II, In addition to meeting the "Qualification Requirements" above, candidates must have one additional year of satisfactory full-time experience working in Assignment Level I; or one additional year of satisfactory full-time experience as described in "1" above.
6. For Assignment to Level III, in addition to meeting the Qualification Requirements for Construction Project Manager, candidates must have two additional years of satisfactory full-time experience working in Construction Project Manager Assignment Level I and II; or two additional years of satisfactory full-time experience as described in question "1" above and possess a motor vehicle driver license valid in the State of New York which must be maintained for the duration of employment noting that if you have moving violations, license suspension or an accident record, you may be disqualified.

title: Redovisningskonsult till kund inom Life Science i Uppsala
description:
Om rollen

Som redovisningskonsult kommer du att ansvara för redovisningsarbetet och säkerställa att finansiell rapportering håller hög kvalitet. Du blir en viktig del av ekonomifunktionen och arbetar nära verksamheten i en organisation med höga kvalitetskrav och stort fokus på utveckling.

Rollen kräver att du är självgående, strukturerad och trivs med att ta ansvar för hela redovisningsprocessen. Du har lätt för att samarbeta med olika intressenter och bidrar gärna med förbättringsförslag och effektiviseringar.

Tjänsten är ett konsultuppdrag där du anställs som konsult av Jurek Talents eller har möjlighet att verka som underkonsult. Uppdraget är långsiktigt och för rätt person finns goda möjligheter till anställning direkt hos kund efter en tids konsultuppdrag. Tjänsten erbjuds på hel- eller deltid och du kommer att sitta på plats hos kund i centrala Uppsala. För rollen tillämpar vi ett lönespann om 38 000–45 000 kr per månad vid heltidsanställning, där placering inom spannet baseras på erfarenhet, kompetens och ansvarsnivå.

Din profil

För att lyckas i rollen ser vi att du är noggrann, ansvarstagande och lösningsorienterad. Du trivs i en föränderlig miljö, har ett proaktivt arbetssätt och motiveras av att skapa struktur och kvalitet i ditt arbete. Vidare ser vi att du;

  • Har eftergymnasial utbildning inom ekonomi eller motsvarande

  • Har flera års erfarenhet av kvalificerat redovisningsarbete

  • Har erfarenhet från redovisningsbyrå och är van vid att hantera flera frågor parallellt

  • Arbetar självständigt med årsbokslut, årsredovisning, deklarationer och rapportering

  • Har goda kunskaper inom svensk redovisning och skattelagstiftning

  • Har god systemvana och lätt för att sätta dig in i nya arbetssätt

Du erbjuds

  • Möjlighet att arbeta brett med kvalificerade redovisningsfrågor och bidra med din expertis i en central roll

  • Kompetenta och engagerade kollegor

  • En flexibel tjänst med möjlighet till deltid eller heltid enligt överenskommelse

  • Mycket goda möjligheter till anställning hos kunden efter avslutat konsultuppdrag för rätt person

Ansökan

Varmt välkommen med din ansökan senast den 30:e september. Vänligen notera att vi inte tar emot ansökningar via email.

För frågor är du varmt välkommen att kontakta ansvarig konsultchef Emelie Prokop via email emelie.prokop@jurek.se

Om Jurek

Jurek är en specialiserad partner inom rekrytering och konsultuthyrning som hjälper företag att hitta rätt kompetens inom Finance, Legal & Compliance, Banking & Insurance, HR och Business support. Vårt erfarna team kombinerar branschkunskap med ett starkt nätverk för att skapa träffsäkra och hållbara matchningar. Vi arbetar långsiktigt, personligt och med hög kvalitet, för att skapa bästa möjliga upplevelse för både kunder och kandidater.

title: Technical Project Manager (Radar Systems)
description:
Are you ready to be part of something big? Our company is building the future of wireless communication - think long-range connectivity, blazing-fast data, ultra-low latency, and unbeatable resistance to interference. As a Technical Project Manager (Radar System), you could be at the heart of this groundbreaking innovation! Imagine researching, designing, and implementing next-gen building a compact, high performance radar system designed to detect and track small UAVs in complex environments, including low attitude, cluttered and urban terrain like never before. If you’re ready to work on real-world problems, push the limits of technology, and leave your mark on the future of connectivity - this is your moment!

Key responsibilities:

  • Management and delivery complex engineering projects and programs, blending technical leadership with structured project and program management.
  • Manage project budgets, resource allocation, risk mitigation, and strategic roadmap planning in alignment with company goals
  • Ability to work across RF, Embedded, FPGA teams and multidisciplinary environments
  • Lead and participate in rigorous design reviews, ensuring appropriate subject matter expert engagement.
  • Work with the Product Owner to define technical requirements
  • Apply strong working knowledge of adjacent disciplines -power electronics, digital electronics, mechanical engineering, and firmware/software to ensure board- and system-level success.
  • Act as a key technical resource: assess and update the company's technology road map, identify key new technical areas for the company.
  • Drive disciplined handoff from engineering to manufacturing through close collaboration with manufacturing engineering, supply chain, and production test engineering.
  • Contributing to or authoring proposals and participating in business capture efforts.

Requirements

  • Bachelors degree in electrical engineering, hardware engineer, aerospace or related field
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressive hardware engineering experience, preferably in aerospace, defence, or regulated manufacturing, including 3 -5 years in leadership/management experience.
  • Experience with MIMO radar or beamforming or automotive radar systems
  • Technical expertise across RF, FPGA, and Embedded
  • Strong leadership skills: ability to understand and collaborate effectively with technical peers, ability to direct the efforts of others, high emotional intelligence with the ability to provide both positive and corrective feedback in a constructive way.
  • Ability to balance technical rigor with execution speed in a fast-paced start up environment.

Benefits

Why KRUSH Labs?

Based in Eindhoven, KRUSH Labs is a privately owned R&D, engineering, and prototyping center where multidisciplinary teams develop next-generation solutions in advanced hardware, embedded systems, wireless communication, sensing, autonomous technologies, AI, and software.

We support the complete innovation journey, from research and proof of concept to rapid prototyping, system integration, validation, and manufacturing readiness. When a solution is proven, we help customers bridge the gap from prototype to pilot production and scalable manufacturing.

Join us to solve complex challenges, take ownership of meaningful work, and help turn ambitious ideas into technologies that make a real-world impact.

title: Practice Leader - Property Risk Consulting
description:
Company:

Marsh

Description:

We are seeking a talented individual to join the Risk Consulting department at Marsh. This role will be based in Sandton, hybrid and has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.

We are seeking a leader to spearhead our Property Risk Consulting (PRC) division, to drive the growth and strategy of this practice in the Africa Risk Consulting business. This role demands a dynamic, visionary leader who can elevate client experience to unparalleled levels, transform team culture into a positive, high-performing environment, and drive sustainable growth and profitability both within existing clients and by sourcing new business opportunities.

The successful candidate will be a master of people leadership, process excellence, and financial stewardship, with a deep understanding of the insurance and risk management landscape, particularly within South Africa’s large corporates.

We will count on you to:

Client Experience & Delivery

  • Champion an exceptional, value-driven client experience that consistently exceeds expectations.
  • Ensure all PRC processes and deliverables are aligned to superior client satisfaction and business outcomes.
  • Build and nurture strong, trusted relationships with key clients, understanding their evolving risk management needs.
  • Lead senior practice involvement on major projects, providing strategic guidance and innovative risk solutions.

Team Culture & Talent Development

  • Drive a cultural towards a positive, collaborative, and high-performance team environment.
  • Inspire, mentor, and develop talent within the PRC team, fostering growth and retention of top performers.
  • Cultivate a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and professional excellence.

Business Growth & Client Development

  • Identify and capitalize on growth opportunities within existing client portfolios.
  • Proactively source and secure new clients, expanding the division’s footprint in the market.
  • Lead business development initiatives, including proposal development, pricing strategies, and market positioning.

Financial & Operational Leadership

  • Own and manage the PRC division’s P&L, ensuring profitable growth and financial discipline.
  • Develop and implement robust processes and controls to optimize operational efficiency and delivery quality.
  • Monitor financial performance against budgets and forecasts, driving revenue and net operating income growth.

What you need to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management, Engineering, Risk, Insurance, or a related field.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in insurance, risk consulting, or related sectors.
  • Proven leadership experience managing teams, ideally including engineers or technical specialists.
  • Deep knowledge of South African insurance markets and experience working with large, listed corporate clients.
  • Demonstrated success in client relationship management, particularly mature clients and dealing with c-suite.
  • Experience in business development, and P&L accountability.
  • Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting.
  • Exceptional people management skills with a high level of emotional intelligence (EQ).
  • Experience in property risk engineering or consulting.

Why join our team:

  • We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
  • We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
  • Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.

Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to embracing a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are also committed to providing reasonable support to any candidate with a disability to allow them to fully participate in the recruitment process. We welcome candidates to contact us at reasonableaccommodations@marsh.com to discuss any specific needs.

Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

title: Trial Division (GCB) - Trial Preparation Assistant, Level II
description:
The Office of the District Attorney, Bronx County (“BXDA”) is charged with the twin goals of ensuring public safety and striving for equal justice for the over 1.4 million members of the Bronx County community. By “Pursuing Justice with Integrity,” the BXDA places a focus on assistance for crime victims while simultaneously ensuring fairness to defendants. Moreover, the BXDA aims to balance the need to seek appropriate punishment for certain crimes while recognizing when punitive measures do not adequately advance justice. By recognizing these significant distinctions and acting accordingly, BXDA has established a standard of excellence in the representation of the Bronx community at large, which continues to grow stronger every day.
In furtherance of this mission, the BXDA seeks experienced and enthusiastic Trial Preparation Assistants in the Trial Division – General Crimes Bureau to aid in all aspects of case preparation from intake to final disposition.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:
Specific duties will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Compile, analyze, redact, and reproduce case documents for discovery compliance and case preparation.
- Preparation and filing of documents.
- Timely retrieval of documents and records.
- Assist in preparing hearing/trial exhibits & discovery for trial.
- Timely conversions of instruments to information.
- Retrieve all necessary documents and records from law enforcement agencies, hospitals and other entitles.
- Produce effective communication with different agencies.
- Locate and retrieve property maintained by NYC Police Dept.
- Perform legal research.
- Engage in witness contact and communication.
- Secure corroborating affidavits
- Prepare orders for Court, including Motion Responses, Legal Memorandums, Search Warrants, Subpoenas, and Orders to Produce.
- Work directly with Assistant District Attorneys (ADAs) on specialty cases.

title: Join our Data Science & AI Talent Community at CommBank
description:
Join our Data Science & AI Talent Community at CommBank

What is the Talent Community?

At CommBank, we’re always looking for people who put customers first and want to use data and AI to solve meaningful problems at scale. Our recruitment is ongoing and never closes — you can join our Data Science & AI Talent Community at any time, and we’ll connect you with relevant opportunities as they arise.

Roles are typically based in Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide or Perth, depending on the team, and sit within our Data Science & AI practice across the Group. Opportunities commonly include Data Scientist, Senior Data Scientist, Chapter Lead/Senior Manager, and Principal Data Scientist roles.

As part of our teams, you’ll build commercial, enterprise‑grade AI solutions that improve productivity, strengthen decision‑making and deliver better customer experiences — while ensuring AI is used responsibly, ethically and at scale for the benefit of customers and the broader Australian community.

Global AI Leadership & Partnerships

At CommBank, you’ll work at the forefront of applied AI through strategic partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic, alongside deep collaboration with the global technology ecosystem. Our Seattle Tech Hub embeds our teams with world‑class technology partners to accelerate capability and deliver real‑world generative and agentic AI solutions at scale. This leadership has been recognised globally, with CommBank ranked #4 worldwide in the 2025 Evident AI Index for AI maturity.

Who we’re looking for

At CommBank, our values of Care, Courage and Commitment guide everything we do – for our customers, our communities and each other. Within Data Science & AI, these values come to life through responsible use of data, ethical AI, and decisions that balance innovation with trust and impact.

We’re building a community of Data Scientists who share these values – people who combine deep technical expertise with strong commercial thinking, leadership capability and purpose. Whether you’re actively looking for your next role or planning a future move, we’d love to hear from people who:

  • Show care by putting customers and community at the heart of data‑driven solutions – acting with integrity, accountability and an ethical mindset focused on customer outcomes, colleagues and key stakeholders.

  • Demonstrate courage through curiosity and sound judgement – excited by tackling new and complex business problems in AI, evolving existing products and capabilities, challenging assumptions and positively influencing senior stakeholders through evidence‑based insight. This includes a strong, curiosity‑led approach to questioning, validating and solving problems using mathematics, statistics and models, and feeling empowered to share thought leadership and problem‑solving ideas in a growing environment that addresses real‑world challenges impacting millions of customers across Australia.

  • Live commitment by investing in continuous learning and craft excellence – bringing deep, hands‑on expertise in Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models (LLMs), with a proven track record of designing, building and delivering end‑to‑end AI capabilities for business stakeholders. This includes strong practical experience implementing Generative AI and agentic and multi‑agent systems, using modern frameworks and tooling such as Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, LangGraph and the OpenAI Responses API, as well as applying a combination of commercial and technical AI models to deliver solutions that create strategic value.

  • Thrive in collaborative environments – working closely with product, engineering and business teams, curious enough to solve real‑world problems, and collaborative in how you design, test and scale AI solutions across the organisation.

  • Feel energised working autonomously and taking ownership – as a self‑motivated, driven leader of work who can effectively collaborate with, support and uplift teams of Data Scientists and AI specialists to deliver high‑quality, scalable outcomes.

  • Connect purpose with impact – contributing to and leading transformational AI initiatives that improve customer outcomes, build trust, and support CommBank’s role in Australia’s long‑term financial wellbeing.

What we offer

  • Flexible opportunities with balance and impact – Enjoy hybrid working that supports both your career and lifestyle, while delivering work that genuinely matters.

  • Deepen your expertise – Work with modern data and AI platforms, tools and frameworks, and tackle complex, high‑impact problems at enterprise scale.

  • Grow your career – Join a strong data science community with clear technical and leadership pathways, mentoring opportunities, and the ability to move across domains and roles.

  • Industry‑leading employee experiences, benefit packages and discounts

  • An inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive
    We welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples, supported by our dedicated Indigenous Careers Team. You’ll also have access to networks that celebrate diversity, foster belonging, and support accessibility requirements and workplace adjustments.

How the process works

  • Apply anytime - Apply using the link, tell us your availability and preferred locations.

  • Talent Acquisition review - If online assessments are successful, our recruitment team will review your experience and may connect with you to assess suitability for current and future Data Science opportunities at CommBank.

  • Talent Community membership - If successful, we’ll confirm your membership in our Talent Community for ongoing engagement for upcoming roles. As an active member, you can move quickly from expressing interest to interview, without needing to re‑apply.

  • Get matched - We’ll reach out when a suitable role opens.

title: Truckförare till kund i Bålsta
description:
Arbetsuppgifter

Är du redo för ett fysiskt aktivt jobb i en viktig bransch? Vi söker dig som vill jobba heltid på ett lager norr om Stockholm – en dynamisk och engagerande tjänst där noggrannhet, samarbete och effektivitet är i fokus! I rollen kommer du att arbeta med flera spännande uppgifter som att registrera inkommande varor i systemet, jämföra leveranser med följesedlar och plocka samt packa kundorder. Du får också chansen att övervaka det automatiserade flödet och robotarna, vilket ger en teknisk twist på ditt arbete. Utöver detta fyller du på varor och kör interna transporter med truck för att säkerställa ett smidigt flöde i lagerprocessen. Det här är jobbet för dig som trivs med fysiskt arbete, gillar att tänka logiskt och vill vara en del av ett team där struktur, kvalitet och samarbete är viktiga nycklar för framgång. Du får värdefull erfarenhet i en bransch som gör skillnad och där du varje dag bidrar till att teamet når sina mål.

Din profil

Vill du ha ett meningsfullt och aktivt jobb där du får vara en del av ett energiskt och stöttande team? Vi söker nu engagerade och noggranna personer till ett lageruppdrag – och vi ser fram emot att välkomna nya kollegor som vill göra skillnad tillsammans med oss! Om tjänsten: I rollen kommer du att arbeta med plock och pack samt andra förekommande uppgifter på lagret. Arbetstiderna är måndag till fredag, antingen dagtid 07:00–16:00 eller kvällspass 14:00–23:00. Tjänsten är på heltid. Vi söker dig som: Är noggrann, flexibel och gillar att ta ansvar Har en positiv attityd och trivs med att arbeta i team Talar och skriver svenska obehindrat Har en drogfri livsstil Det är ett extra plus om du också har: Erfarenhet från lager, särskilt inom utleverans eller godsmottagning B-körkort (Tillgång till bil) Högre truckbehörighet (vi kan stå för truckkort om du inte har det) Vi erbjuder: Ett heltidsjobb där du får vara en del av ett varmt och inkluderande team som stöttar varandra och har kul på jobbet. Vi ser till att du utvecklas, både inom logistik och i arbetslivet generellt, samtidigt som du får vara med och bidra till ett företag där vi bryr oss om varandra. Vi arbetar aktivt för att skapa en inkluderande arbetsplats och strävar efter en balanserad könsfördelning i våra team.

title: Oliver Wyman – Entry-level Consultant (m/f/d) 2027– Stockholm
description:
Company:

Oliver Wyman

Description:

Who we are

Oliver Wyman is a global management consulting firm. We work with clients through their most defining moments, combining deep industry knowledge, specialized expertise, and the power of perspective to help them adapt, grow, and thrive.

We believe diverse perspectives make the work stronger. Our consultants bring different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to help solve complex problems and create lasting impact for clients, colleagues, and communities.

At Oliver Wyman, we are proud of the values that we aspire to live by. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.

What you will do

  • As a member of your project team you’ll work alongside colleagues of all levels and clients worldwide to solve complex problems and drive meaningful change.

  • You’ll help teams understand client challenges by conducting research, gathering data, running surveys and interviews, and turning information into clear insights.

  • You’ll analyze problems, identify patterns, test hypotheses, and help structure recommendations that support client decision-making.

  • You’ll contribute to client-ready deliverables, including presentations, analysis, workshops, and discussions that help move projects forward.

  • You’ll have the opportunity to work across our industries and capabilities, with the flexibility to specialize early or explore different areas before choosing a path.

  • You’ll likely have the chance to travel within your home market and internationally. No two weeks are ever the same.

  • You’ll build core consulting skills from the start, including how to structure your work, communicate clearly, contribute to team problem-solving, and manage your priorities.

Why join us?

You can be your best here. At Oliver Wyman, you will find meaningful work, talented people, and a culture built on trust, support, and growth.

Create solutions that have impact

  • Work on challenging projects that help clients solve complex problems, make better decisions, and create meaningful impact.

  • Have the opportunity to work across different industries, capabilities, and cultures, contributing to work that has lasting impact for clients, industries, and society.

  • Be part of teams that measure success not just by deliverables, but by the difference created together.

Develop as a leader

  • From day one, be encouraged to take initiative, ask questions, and bring your perspective to the work.

  • Learn how to structure problems, communicate clearly, and contribute to team discussions and client conversations.

  • As you grow, you’ll have opportunities to build confidence, take on more responsibility, and develop the skills to unlock the potential of others.

Learn and grow without limits

  • Learn on the job and through formal training, developing core skills in communication, presentation, analytics, problem-solving, and client management.

  • Each project will give you new opportunities to learn from specialists, broaden your perspective, and build momentum in your career.

  • You’ll have support around you as you grow, including a dedicated buddy, a career advisor, your talent manager, and communities that help you find your place.

Thrive in a vibrant and inclusive culture

  • Work with genuine colleagues who stand by their beliefs, collaborate across differences, and support one another.

  • Be part of an open, inclusive, and down-to-earth culture where diverse perspectives strengthen the work.

  • Connect with colleagues through employee resource groups, office communities, and social activities.

Experience rewards that work for you

  • We believe in flexibility, including hybrid working, and in helping colleagues build sustainable careers.

  • Over time, you’ll have access to opportunities, programs, and experiences designed to help you perform, grow, and thrive — including non-profit fellowships, sabbaticals, and externships.

  • Enjoy competitive local benefits designed to support your well-being, development, and life outside of work.

Who can apply?

  • Applicants with a Bachelor´s (and Master’s) degree only are eligible to apply for this vacancy.

  • We look for people who display initiative, intuition, and creativity with a strong problem solving and analytical mindset. We do not require specific academic majors or industry experience; we value diversity of experience and skills, extracurricular activities, and evidence of leading an interesting and impactful life outside of your studies.

  • Language skills: Swedish or another Scandinavian language and English (native/fluent).

How to apply?

Please submit your CV, cover letter and transcripts. If you would like to find out more information about Oliver Wyman, please visit our website or alternatively, apply to attend one of our events, details of which can be found here.

What to expect during the interviews process?

At Oliver Wyman, we want you to shine in your interview. Our process is designed like our work environment — it’s challenging, exciting, and fun.

With a mix of conversational and case interviews, our approach not only helps us to get to know you better, understanding your strengths and interests, but it also enables you to learn more about our people and our business.

If you want to learn more about consulting interviews and start your preparation, please visit our careers page: https://www.oliverwyman.com/careers/entry-level/interview-preparation.html

Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

title: Hazardous Materials Specialist
description:
THE AGENCY
The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expand housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability.

DCP supports the City Planning Commission in its annual review of hundreds of land use applications. The Department also advises on citywide strategic and capital planning, analyzes data, conducts policy analysis, and creates open data and civic engagement tools.

The Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Department values public service, collaboration, and creativity, and supports professional development. Learn more about DCP at www.nyc.gov/planning.

THE DIVISION
The Environmental Assessment and Review Division (EARD) is responsible for preparing and reviewing City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR) applications for the City Planning Commission. The Division coordinates the review of CEQR applications between DCP and other government agencies and conducts CEQR reviews, including the review and preparation of draft and final Environmental Impact Statements. In addition, the Division prepares final CEQR determinations, letters and memos; and provides technical assistance in the preparation and submission of applications.

THE ROLE
The Division is seeking a Hazardous Materials Specialist with expertise in site investigation and remediation to support the preparation, analysis and review of CEQR applications, with a focus on Hazardous Materials analyses. The position is an opportunity to work closely with DCP staff throughout the agency, interagency CEQR teams, and project teams to analyze and disclose potential environmental impacts related to discretionary land use actions. The candidate should possess strong communication and problem-solving skills; an ability to grasp complex policy issues; and a desire to contribute to an engaging, collaborative team environment.

Under the supervision of the Deputy Director and Director, with wide latitude for independent judgment, the candidate will be expected to perform work including – but not limited to – the following:

- Review technical reports, such as Phase I Environmental Site Assessments (ESA), Phase II/Subsurface/Remedial Investigations and Hazardous Materials sections of CEQR environmental assessments;
- Discern and design hazardous materials environmental requirements for zoning actions including the (e) designation process;
- Provide clear guidance to EARD staff and CEQR applicants to aid in the preparation and submission of Hazardous Materials analyses to the department;
- Coordinate inter- and intra- agency technical reviews related to the preparation and review of CEQR applications. Liaise with Hazardous Materials technical experts at partner agencies including the NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) and the Mayor’s Office of Environmental Remediation (OER);
- Conduct meetings to resolve issues and recommend solution strategies aligned with the mission and strategic priorities of the Department;
- Communicate effectively with staff and other stakeholders, as needed;
- Perform related tasks.

TO APPLY:
Please visit: https://www1.nyc.gov/jobs/ and follow the steps below:
1. Search for job ID number: 793919
2. Click on the job business title: Hazardous Materials Specialist
3. Click on “Apply Now” at the bottom of the posting

title: DIRECTOR OF PROCEDURES
description:
APPLICANTS MUST BE PERMANENT IN THE ADMINISTRATIVE STAFF ANALYST TITLE OR BE PERMANENT IN A COMPARABLE TITLE ELIGIBLE FOR 6.1.9 TITLE CHANGE.

The Department of Social Services (DSS) is comprised of the administrative units of the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) and the Department of Homeless Services (DHS). HRA is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance. DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self-sufficiency as quickly as possible.

The Office of Procedures provides the critical link between policy development and worker execution of the agency programs. Up-to-date, well-written procedures, supported with effective training, provide workers with the knowledge and standards required to operate agency's program consistently and effectively.

Reporting to the Senior Director, with wide latitude for independent judgement and initiative, the Director is responsible for planning, coordinating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating procedures designed for DSS/HRA/DHS staff. The Director applies a set of processes, tools, techniques, and skills necessary to successfully execute projects on time within budget, while managing the Agency’s expectations. The Director advises, confers and meets with all senior staff, including Divisions Directors, Assistant Deputy Commissioners and Deputy Commissioners and other staff as necessary. The Director is the primary point of contact for communications, interpretation and development of procedures related to Department of Social Services (DHS) Homeless Prevention Administration (HPA) and the Fair Fares program.

The Office of Policy, Procedures and Training (OPPT) is recruiting for one (1) Administrative Staff Analyst NM-I to function as a Director of Procedures who will:

- Direct and coordinate a procedure unit in the development, composition and editing of written policies and procedures including directives; manuals; operational instructions; charts; graphs and memorandums. Oversee the research of current and historic federal, state and city legislation regulations, court orders and settlements to ensure the composition of accurate and timely policy and procedures. Ensure that all policies and procedures are compliant with Agency policies and regulatory and statute requirements.

- Work closely with DSS/HRA/DHS Operational Directors and Executive staff to review drafts and existing operational and fiscal policies and procedures. Discuss operations and maintains a list of necessary policies and procedures; meet weekly to oversee and discuss the status of the unit's ongoing and pending assignments.

- Manage the development and implementation of special initiatives and operational reviews including the development of project plans, policies and procedures, monitoring implementation, document review, tracking, and operational and fiscal impact analyses.

- Ensure that all policies and procedures comply with Agency policies and regulatory requirements and oversee the maintenance and the integrity of the repositories for the publishing of documents. Manages the tracking, posting and distribution of policy and procedural documents.

- Liaise with DSS/HRA/DHS program areas for the coordination of joint initiatives, policies and procedures. Ensure that necessary revisions to existing DSS/HRA/DHS procedures are completed in accordance with joint initiatives, requirements, and processes.

- Supervise procedure writers in multiple, complex research projects including analysis of social services legislation, regulation and operational trends. Reviews and approves policy documents and related materials to standardize formats and identify and direct the resolution of procedural inconsistencies. Assure written communication efforts are consistent with and lead to the maximum realization of the objectives of the Agency management plan.

- Attend Agency meetings on behalf of the Senior Director and informs senior Agency members of new information. Interact with other Agencies and advises in high level staff meetings where the development and implementation of procedural documents are discussed and determined.

- Coordinate, assign and direct ad hoc assignment and troubleshoot for the Senior Director as requested.
